summary: MontclairHealth streaming blackout causing fallback amplification and customer escalation
summary_short: Morning streaming blackout caused silent failover to degraded model, duplicate completions, and billing exposure
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-11 07:12 UTC Montclair Health experienced a region-wide streaming blackout for production requests routed to us-east. Long-lived streaming connections dropped silently and the request router triggered fallback rules that redirected traffic to smaller quantized variants, amplifying tail latency and producing duplicate/incoherent completions for a subset of requests. Customer began escalating at 07:30 UTC citing truncated clinical transcripts and inconsistent patient summary outputs.

Impact:
- Affected ~18% of Montclair Health's traffic for 31 minutes (07:12–07:43 UTC).
- 5xx spike to 12% across streaming endpoints; synchronous completion endpoints saw a 4x latency increase for long-context calls.
- Several calls fell back to open-7b-v1 and open-13b-v2-quant; customers reported hallucinated medication entries in 2% of returned transcripts.
- Billing exposure: duplicate completions and replayed fragments led to estimated 6k token overcount for Montclair's account during the window.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster behind streaming-proxy v2.1.1 and api-gateway v3.8.
- Autoscaler configured with headroom policy: min_inflight_headroom=0.18, burst_enabled=true.

Steps to reproduce (investigative):
1) Simulate a high-fanout streaming workload with persistent 30s prefix followed by large completion (seq_len 2048) using Montclair's production prompt set.
2) Inject intermittent TCP resets at proxy layer (simulated network jitter) and observe router behavior when connections fail mid-KV-stream.
3) Observe fallback decision path: router reassigns to quantized variant when latency > 2.2s or 429s exceed threshold.

Logs / observed traces (snippets):
- streaming-proxy: "2026-03-11T07:12:05Z WARN conn=xyz reset-by-peer; pending-frames=3"
- router: "fallback: reason=connection_reset; target=open-13b-v2-quant; trace_id=abc123"
- serving-runtime: "2026-03-11T07:12:27Z ERROR tokenization_mismatch: prompt_chunk=8; kv_miss=1"
- billing: "2026-03-11T07:43:05Z NOTICE duplicate-completion-detected count=187 estimated_tokens=6120 account=montclair-health"
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 07:12 UTC first proxy resets observed; 07:15 UTC SRE alerted via #support; 07:20 UTC customer CS rep engaged; 07:30 UTC customer began escalating to CSM and APAC ops. Root cause hypothesis: connection pooling at streaming-proxy failed to gracefully drain when upstream transient TCP resets occurred, triggering abrupt connection closures and leaving inflight streams in indeterminate state. Router logic interpreted closed connections as instance failure and executed fallback amplification across multiple routers because of stale affinity cache. Secondary factor: autoscaler headroom was tightly tuned for cost, which reduced available capacity for rapid fallback handling leading to queuing and duplicate retried attempts.

Key evidence: proxy logs show a 1.9s median reconnect loop for affected frontends; affinity cache TTL was set to 15s and had a stale entry spike during the incident. No disk or GPU OOMs found on serving nodes.

Temporary mitigations performed during incident: rolled back streaming-proxy to v2.0.8 in the affected availability zone (07:34 UTC) which restored graceful connection teardown; increased router affinity cache clear frequency; temporarily increased autoscaler headroom to 0.35 to reduce immediate failovers.
resolution_notes:
Fixes applied:
- Reverted streaming-proxy to 2.0.8 in us-east and queued a canary for 2.1.2 with an additional connection-drain patch (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/428).
- Updated router fallback policy to require two consecutive connection failures before mass fallback (config change rolled at 08:10 UTC).
- Raised autoscaler min_inflight_headroom to 0.35 and adjusted burst window to 60s.
- Issued a billing credit to Montclair Health for token overcount (credit amount: $1,320) and opened an invoice reconciliation ticket with finance (linked).

Follow-up action items (owners and due dates):
- Eng/SRE to implement connection-drain observability metrics and alert (Owner: Marcus Li, due 2026-03-18).
- Runtime team to add deterministic replay-detection to prevent duplicate token counting during abrupt disconnects (Owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-04-01).
- Support to update post-incident customer-facing summary and confirm acceptance of billing credit (Owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-14).
- Product to revisit autoscaler default headroom recommendation for streaming customers and publish guidance (Owner: Lina Martinez, due 2026-03-25).
final_communication: Customer update sent 2026-03-13: apologized for impact, summarized actions and credit offered, scheduled technical review with Montclair engineering team for 2026-03-16. Customer acknowledged and requested a follow-up on waveform logs and a copy of the new router config. CSM accepted and follow-up meeting scheduled.

2026-03-11T07:40Z - Priya Rao (Runtime): Confirmed fallback amplification due to router affinity TTL spike; quantized variants handled significantly more fanout than expected. Opening PR to require double-failure before fallback. See PR #428.

2026-03-12T10:14Z - Lina Martinez (Product): Will include recommended headroom defaults for streaming customers in next week's release notes. Drafted guidance and shared with SRE for review.
